name: PATCH /api/sla/policies/:id - Adjust an SLA policy
description: Partially updates an SLA policy. Answers 200 - an update to an existing resource, not a creation. A PARTIAL update: only the keys present in the body are written, so an operator correcting a typo in the name cannot accidentally reset the target. Absence and null are DIFFERENT for source_channel: omitting it leaves the channel alone, while an explicit null turns a channel-specific policy into the catch-all, which is a meaningful configuration change. At least one field must be present - an empty patch is a caller mistake worth reporting rather than a silent no-op. Tightening a target does NOT retroactively re-judge leads already in flight: a lead's sla_due_at was written at assignment from the policy in force at that moment, and moving the goalposts under somebody working a queue would manufacture breaches nobody could have prevented. New policies apply to leads assigned after the change. Setting is_active true revives a retired policy - retirement is reversible because the row is never destroyed. Protected - SLA targets decide when somebody is judged late. QA: depends on register, login and a created policy.

testCases.name: Relax the target and rename the policy

errorCases.when: the id path parameter is not a well-formed UUID, no updatable field is supplied, name is blank or over 160 characters, source_channel is neither null nor one of the fourteen channels, first_response_minutes is not an integer between 1 and 10080, business_hours_only or is_active is not a boolean, or evaluation_order is not an integer between 0 and 100000
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
no SLA policy exists with the supplied id
the change would leave two ACTIVE policies on the same source_channel at the same evaluation_order, which would make the effective SLA depend on insertion order
